introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0760 HISTORY 1, JUNE 2026, ADVANCED LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, Duration: One and a Half Hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the question booklet is headed "Advanced Level - 0760 History 1". Answer ALL the 50 questions in this Examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide on which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the Answer Sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; if you find a question difficult, move on to the next question and come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet, using, where necessary, the blank spaces in the question booklet.
incertitudes: Sujet scanné (filigrane gcerevision.com sans conséquence sur la lisibilité) de 6 pages : page de garde (History 1, 0760, JUNE 2026, ADVANCED LEVEL, vérifiés), puis 50 QCM sur les pages 2 à 6 (Q1-11, 12-21, 22-32, 33-42, 43-50). Aucun corrigé officiel ni clé imprimée : toutes les réponses sont établies d'après l'historiographie courante, sans source consultable pendant la transcription ; aucune statistique ni citation n'est avancée.

Page de garde : instructions 6 à 11 et exemple de marquage recopiés dans `introduction_markdown`, sans les champs administratifs (centre, candidat) ni les mentions de page. Publicités et filigranes ignorés.

Questions converties en ouvertes, sans lettre retenue, faute de pouvoir départager les options ou de pouvoir vérifier le fait : Q1 (paires de royaumes nés de querelles dynastiques non établies), Q6 (aucune liste des termes du traité germano-duala de 1884 ne permet d'identifier l'exception), Q10 (crise de 1953 : plusieurs options défendables), Q11 (cause immédiate de l'insurrection UPC : l'épisode de la taxe sur les étals de Yaoundé n'a pu être vérifié), Q13 (C et D se défendent comme exception), Q16 (« Train Affair » de 1962 non vérifiable, même point que dans le sujet 2024), Q20 (admission au Commonwealth, sommet de l'OUA et règlement de Bakassi se rattachent tous à l'ère Biya), Q25 (B et D se défendent), Q29 (A, B et C se défendent), Q39 (aucune option ne dit l'objectif réel, empêcher l'alliance franco-russe), Q41 (A et B se défendent), Q48 (A et C se défendent comme bénéfice économique).

Q24 : le Berlin Act ne partageait pas l'Afrique (partage fait ensuite par traités bilatéraux), mais il ne réglait pas non plus l'expansion vers l'arrière-pays (C) : D est donnée comme « Intended answer » (exception la plus conventionnelle), question laissée ouverte pour autoévaluation.

Réponses retenues avec un degré de certitude moyen (à relire par un historien avant mise en ligne) : Q2 A (les Duala avaient des chefs héréditaires), Q3 A (C, le fulfulde, est une conséquence voisine), Q5 D (B, la révolution industrielle, est la cause générale de la course à l'Afrique), Q7 C (D, abolition de la traite, est écartée car la traite et le travail forcé ont subsisté), Q9 C (B, absence de budget séparé, en est une conséquence), Q14 B (D, protection des deux cultures, est voisine), Q17 B (A est la version officielle), Q22 B (A, les langues locales, est un facteur voisin), Q26 C (B, la solidarité, est liée), Q31 B (C, la Communauté française de 1958, est aussi des années 1950), Q47 B (A et D, absence de force permanente et de moyens, sont des difficultés réelles).

Q12 : le Haut-Commissaire de France en 1957-1958 était Jean Ramadier ; l'option B est donc exacte (le sujet 2023 doutait de ce nom). Q15 : Jua a été remplacé par Muna en 1968 (date retenue d'après le sujet). Q18 : poste de Premier ministre créé en 1975, successeur constitutionnel du Président depuis 1979 (Biya succède en novembre 1982).

Faits datés cités dans les corrigés, d'après l'historiographie courante : traité germano-duala du 12 juillet 1884 ; Berlin Act du 26 février 1885 ; condominium de 1914, partage de 1916, Déclaration Milner-Simon du 10 juillet 1919 ; référendum du 20 mai 1972 ; accession de Biya le 6 novembre 1982 ; coup d'État du 6 avril 1984 ; admission au Commonwealth (1995), sommet de l'OUA à Yaoundé (1996), arrêt de la CIJ (2002), retrait nigérian de Bakassi (2008) ; Loi-Cadre du 23 juin 1956 ; indépendance du Ghana le 6 mars 1957 ; Adowa le 1er mars 1896 ; traité de réassurance de juin 1887 ; Locarno 1925 ; ligne directe de 1963. Aucune citation, statistique ni source inventée.

Défauts d'impression du sujet : aucune clé imprimée ; « Frist World War » (Q41) ; « London Baptist Missionary Society » (Q4, la société s'appelle Baptist Missionary Society, de Londres) ; « paganic Islamic practices » (Q23) ; « Maroua Accord » (Q20, usuellement Déclaration de Maroua, 1975, antérieure au régime Biya) ; « Secret Reinsurance Treaty » (Q39) entre l'Allemagne et la Russie, alors que l'option B parle d'alliés « Russia and Serbia » ; Q43 : énoncé « was: » sans fin de phrase ; Q43-Q45 dates et espacements irréguliers (« 1950 -1953 ») recopiés ; plusieurs options sans point final et un espace avant le point dans Q2 et Q12, normalisés ; Q31 : « Legislative Assemblies » imprécis (assemblées territoriales) ; Q18 option B imprimée « the re-establishment the post of Prime Minister » (« of » manquant, recopié tel quel).
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 1, 6, 10, 11, 13, 16, 20, 24, 25, 29, 39, 41, 48.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Dynastic quarrels were responsible for the migration of the:

*Options as printed:* A) Kom and Bafut Kingdoms.   B) Ewondo and Bakweri Chiefdoms.   C) Bamum and Nso Kingdoms.   D) Bafut and Bamum Kingdoms.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A dynastic quarrel is a dispute over succession to a throne or a chiefdom. In the Grassfields and the surrounding forest, a defeated claimant often left with his followers and founded a new chiefdom, and this is one of the recognised causes of migration in pre-colonial Cameroon, next to wars, population pressure, the search for land and the Fulani and Chamba raids. Several Grassfields kingdoms trace their origin to the Tikar and to splits of this kind, so more than one of the printed pairs can be defended, and the details of each kingdom's migration are not settled in the sources available here. No letter is retained.

A full answer names the cause (a succession dispute), gives one or two examples of chiefdoms founded by a breakaway prince and distinguishes this cause from the others (wars, search for land, population pressure).



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The coastal and forest states in pre-colonial Cameroon were commonly described as non-centralised societies because of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A non-centralised (or acephalous) society has no single ruler holding authority over a wide territory. Power is shared among heads of lineages, village councils and associations such as secret societies, and there is no fixed class of rulers set above a class of subjects. Option A describes this lack of a marked social hierarchy.

The other options do not define the type: these societies did have leaders (family and lineage heads, councils), so C is false; secret societies (for example Ngbe or Ekpe) were present and even important in them, so B is false; and patrilineal succession is a rule of inheritance that is found in centralised kingdoms too (D).

Caution: some coastal peoples, such as the Duala, had hereditary chiefs, so the description fits most but not all of the coastal and forest societies.

**Answer: A.**
themes: pre-colonial peoples and states of cameroon

choix.texte: the absence of social stratification.
the absence of secret societies.
the absence of leaders.
the practice of patrilineal succession.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important outcome of the Fulani Jihads of the 19th century in North Cameroon was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The jihads of the 19th century, begun in the Sokoto region by Usman dan Fodio and carried into Adamawa by Modibbo Adama, ended with the Fulani ruling the non-Muslim peoples of Adamawa and the north (grouped under the name Kirdi) through lamidates (such as Ngaoundere, Tibati, Banyo and Rey Bouba). The main outcome was therefore political: Fulani domination (hegemony).

The spread of Fulfulde (C) and the access to pasture (B) followed from that domination, and the purification of Islam (D) was a motive of the jihad rather than an outcome that can be measured.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the advent of Fulani hegemony.
the acquisition of grazing land.
advent of Fulfulde as dominant language.
the purification of Islam.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major limitation of the London Baptist Missionary Society activities in Cameroon before 1884 was that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Baptist missionaries, who began work on the Cameroon coast in the 1840s, had their stations at Bimbia, Douala and Victoria (and on Fernando Po). Because of disease, the lack of transport and the hostility or reserve of some peoples, they hardly entered the interior before the German annexation of 1884. Their limitation was therefore geographical (B).

The other options are false: they bought land for Victoria rather than seizing most of the land (A), they opened schools (C), and they built mission houses, chapels and a printing press (D).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: they expropriated most of the indigenous lands.
their activities were limited to the coastal settlements.
they failed to open any educational institutions.
they did not carry out any infrastructural development.

questions.enonce_markdown: The upsurge in European activities along the Cameroon coast resulting in the scramble for the territory was principally sparked off by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the Cameroon coast, British traders and missionaries had been established since the early 19th century, and from the 1860s and 1870s German firms (Woermann, Jantzen and Thormaehlen) challenged them in the trade with the Duala middlemen. The rivalry between these firms pushed the traders to ask their governments for protection, and the Duala chiefs themselves asked Britain for a protectorate. Germany signed the treaty with the Duala chiefs on 12 July 1884, a few days before the British consul Hewett arrived.

The Industrial Revolution, the need for raw materials and the search for markets (A, B, C) are the general background of the European scramble for Africa, but the immediate spark in Cameroon was the commercial rivalry between European traders.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the search for raw materials.
the Industrial Revolution
the search for markets
commercial rivalry among European traders

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following were the terms of the Germano-Duala Treaty of July 1884 EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) the respect of the middleman monopoly in trade   B) the respect of native rights over their land   C) payment of yearly dues to the chiefs.   D) the respect of former treaties of friendship and commerce.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The treaty was signed on 12 July 1884 between the Duala chiefs (the kings of Bell and Akwa) and the representatives of the German firms Woermann and Jantzen and Thormaehlen, acting for the German Empire. The chiefs gave up sovereignty, legislative power and administration, and in return the usual lists of the terms mention respect for the land cultivated by the Duala and their burial places, the payment of yearly dues (the comey) to the chiefs, and the maintenance of local customs and of their trade as middlemen with the interior. Lists found in textbooks differ from one another, and I could not confirm which one of the four printed items was not in the treaty. No letter is retained.

A full answer lists the terms that are certain (land rights, annual dues, customs, role of the Duala in trade), the cession of sovereignty, and the later German failure to respect the middleman role.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A political achievement of the Germans in Cameroon was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for a political (not economic or social) achievement. The Germans fixed the frontiers of Kamerun by treaties with their neighbours (with Britain towards Nigeria in 1893, 1906 and 1913 and with France in 1894 and 1911, which added the territory known as Neukamerun) and had the boundaries surveyed and mapped. This is a political and administrative achievement that survived their rule and shaped the later frontiers of the country.

Modern industries (A) were few, since the German economy in Cameroon rested on plantations and trade; western-type education (B) was social and was left mostly to the missions; and slave trade and forced labour did not simply disappear under German rule (D).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the establishment of modern industries.
the introduction of western-type education.
the mapping of the boundaries of Cameroon.
the abolition of slave trade in the country.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most significant consequence of the failure of the proposed Condominium in Cameroon during the First World War was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the fall of Douala in September 1914, Britain and France tried to run the occupied territory together as a condominium, a joint administration. It failed because of disagreements between the two allies on the way to administer the territory and on their respective shares. When the German resistance ended in early 1916 the two powers divided the territory between them: a first partition was made in 1916, confirmed by the Milner-Simon Declaration of 10 July 1919 and later by the League of Nations mandates. The Anglo-French partition is the most important consequence.

The other options are not consequences of the failure of the condominium: the force of the allies was formed at the start of the campaign (A), the subjection of Cameroonians to two cultures was a result of the partition and not of the failure itself (B), and the German resistance ended in 1916 (C).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the creation of the West African Expeditionary Force.
the subjection of Cameroonians to the English and French cultures.
the prolonged German resistance against the Allies.
the Anglo-French partition of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: The minimal economic advancement in British Southern Cameroons during the Mandate era was mainly attributed to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under the League of Nations mandate (1922-1946) and the trusteeship that followed, Britain administered the Southern Cameroons as a part of Nigeria. The territory was treated as a distant appendage: the money, the roads, the schools and the hospitals went first to the Nigerian regions, and Southern Cameroons had little capital and little attention. This administrative arrangement is the main reason for its slow development.

The lack of a separate budget (B) is a consequence of that arrangement rather than a separate cause; there were plenty of raw materials, such as palm produce, rubber and timber (D); and the territory was not spared taxation to protect British citizens (A).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the unwillingness to over tax British citizens.
the absence of a separate budget.
the administration of the territory as part of Nigeria.
the shortage of raw materials.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most important political impact of the 1953 Eastern Regional Crisis on Southern Cameroonians was:

*Options as printed:* A) the formation of political parties.   B) the formation of the Benevolent Neutrality.   C) the organisation of the Mamfe Conference.   D) the split among the Southern Cameroons politicians.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In 1953 a split within the NCNC in the Eastern Region of Nigeria led to a political crisis in the Eastern House of Assembly, in which the Southern Cameroons members, among them E.M.L. Endeley, were involved. Their dissatisfaction with the way Southern Cameroons was treated in the Eastern Region led them to demand a separate status, and in 1954 Southern Cameroons was given a quasi-federal status with its own House of Assembly at Buea. Southern Cameroons conferences, among them the one at Mamfe, and the policy of "benevolent neutrality" in Nigerian party politics belong to this period.

Several of the printed options can be linked to the crisis, and I could not confirm which one the examiners regard as the most important political impact. No letter is retained.

A full answer explains the crisis, its effect on the attitude of the Southern Cameroons leaders and the move towards separation from the Eastern Region in 1954.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The immediate cause of the UPC uprising against the French colonial administration in the 1950s was:

*Options as printed:* A) the harassment of UPC supporters.   B) the ban on the UPC newspapers.   C) the ban on UPC rallies.   D) the 100 per cent rise in daily tax for market stalls in Yaounde.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC), founded in 1948 and led by Ruben Um Nyobe, demanded reunification and independence and was in constant conflict with the French administration. In May 1955 serious riots broke out in Douala, Yaounde and other towns, and in July 1955 the UPC and its allied organisations were banned and its leaders went underground; the armed struggle in the Sanaga-Maritime forests followed. The measures taken by the administration against UPC meetings and activists before the riots are generally given as the immediate cause, but I could not confirm which of the four printed measures the examiners have in mind, and the tax episode in Yaounde in option D could not be verified. No letter is retained.

A full answer separates the long-term causes (colonial repression, the refusal of reunification and independence), the immediate causes of the riots of May 1955 and the consequences (ban, maquis).



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: French contribution to the fall of Andre-Marie Mbida in 1958 could be attributed mainly to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Andre-Marie Mbida became Prime Minister of French Cameroon in 1957. In February 1958 several of his ministers resigned together and his government fell, and Ahmadou Ahidjo became Prime Minister. The French High Commissioner of the time, Jean Ramadier, is held to have encouraged and organised these resignations because Mbida had become an obstacle to the French plans for the territory. This is the French contribution to his fall (B).

The other options are reproaches addressed to Mbida by his opponents, not an action by France.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Mbida's rejection of the French solution to the UPC crisis.
Ramadier organised the mass resignation of Mbida's ministers.
the rejection of the reunification of Cameroon by Mbida.
the threat to the unity of French Cameroon by Mbida's government.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The victory of the KNDP in the 1959 elections in Southern Cameroons against the KNC/KPP alliance was a consequence of the following factors EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) the contour ploughing farming laws of the KNC government.   B) the arrogance of the KNC/KPP alliance.   C) the unpopularity of the KNC/KPP alliance.   D) the fear of Igbo domination.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the elections of January 1959 for the Southern Cameroons House of Assembly, the KNDP of J.N. Foncha narrowly defeated the KNC (Endeley) and KPP alliance. The reasons usually given are the unpopular farming regulations (the contour ploughing laws) enforced by the KNC government, the arrogance of the leaders of the alliance and the KNDP's appeal against domination by Nigerians, especially the Igbo, and for a Cameroons of their own. The unpopularity of the alliance (C) is more a description of the result than a separate cause, while the fear of Igbo domination (D) was a real element of the campaign; the question can therefore be read in two ways and I could not determine which option the examiners regard as the exception. No letter is retained.

A full answer lists the causes (contour ploughing laws, arrogance of the alliance, the KNDP programme, anti-Nigerian feeling) and the importance of the result for the 1961 plebiscite.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The adoption of federalism as a new form of government for Cameroon in 1961 was principally induced by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the Foumban Constitutional Conference of July 1961, the leaders of Southern Cameroons, J.N. Foncha above all, asked for a federal constitution because the Southern Cameroons was a small minority (roughly a fifth of the population of the new state) with its own English-language legal and political heritage, and they feared being swallowed up in a unitary French-speaking state. Federalism was therefore a guarantee for the Anglophone minority (B). Ahidjo would have preferred a unitary state and accepted the federal formula as a concession (A is therefore false).

The re-unification itself (C) is the event that needed a constitution, not the reason for the choice of federalism. The safeguarding of the two cultures (D) is closely linked to B, but it is the Anglophone minority that demanded the guarantee, and B is the more exact answer.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Ahidjo's support for federalism
the protection of the minority Anglophones.
the 1961 re-unification.
the safeguarding of French and English cultures.

questions.enonce_markdown: Muna succeeded Jua as Prime Minister of West Cameroon in 1968 mainly because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A.N. Jua, Prime Minister of West Cameroon from 1965, was dismissed in 1968 by President Ahidjo, who wanted a Prime Minister who would work for the centralisation of the federation. S.T. Muna, who had backed the Ahidjo-led national party and the plans of the President, was named in his place. It was Ahidjo's choice and it rested on Muna's support for his ambitions (D).

Muna's earlier career (A) is not the reason for his appointment; the financial problems (B) and the party rivalries (C) existed, but the decisive factor was the wish of the President.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: he had a rich political career in West Cameroon.
the financial situation in West Cameroon was very bad.
of the political rivalry among political parties in West Cameroon.
of his support for Ahidjo's ambitions.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Catholic newspaper, l'Effort Camerounais was sanctioned in East Cameroon in 1962 because:

*Options as printed:* A) of its attempts to uncover the 'Train Affair'.   B) it defended the 'Gang of Four' against Ahidjo.   C) it published favourable articles on the UPC.   D) of its challenge on the Federal Constitution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
L'Effort Camerounais was the newspaper of the Catholic Church in French Cameroon, and in the early years of the federation (1961-1962) the Ahidjo government was increasingly hostile to critics in the press. I could not verify the episode called the "Train Affair" nor the exact reason for the sanction against this newspaper in 1962, so none of the printed options can be confirmed. No letter is retained.

A full answer places the sanction in the context of the growing control of the press and of the opposition under Ahidjo (the arrest of political opponents in 1962, the ban on parties and the single party in 1966).



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The federal system of government was successfully abolished in Cameroon in 1972 principally because of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The federation was replaced by the United Republic of Cameroon after the referendum of 20 May 1972. Ahidjo had prepared the change for years: the parties were merged into a single party (the Cameroon National Union, 1966), the powers of the federated states were reduced step by step, the leaders of West Cameroon were divided and set against one another, and the opposition was kept under control. His political skill and control of allies and rivals is the main explanation (B).

The official reading (A) is that the people asked for unity, but the referendum took place in a one-party system without a real choice. The infighting in West Cameroon (C) was a tool the President used rather than a problem he ended, and there was no agreement with Foncha on the creation of a unitary state (D).

**Answer: B.**
themes: creation of the united republic of cameroon

choix.texte: the interest manifested by Cameroonians in a unitary form of government.
President Ahidjo's ability to manipulate his political allies and rivals.
the ability of President Ahidjo to end the political infighting in West Cameroon.
agreements reached by Ahidjo and Foncha on the creation of a unitary government.

questions.enonce_markdown: The 1979 Constitutional amendment in the United Republic of Cameroon resulted in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The post of Prime Minister was created in 1975 (Paul Biya was appointed to it), when the post of Vice President was abolished. The constitutional amendment of 1979 made the Prime Minister the constitutional successor of the President in case of vacancy of the presidency. This is how Paul Biya came to succeed Ahidjo when he resigned in November 1982.

The post was created in 1975, not re-established in 1979 (B), and the Vice Presidency had been abolished earlier (D). The President of the National Assembly was not placed second in command (C).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the Prime Minister as the constitutional successor to the President.
the re-establishment the post of Prime Minister.
the President of the National Assembly as the second in command to the President.
the abolition of the post of Vice President.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major political problem that threatened the government of President Paul Biya shortly after his accession to power was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Paul Biya became President on 6 November 1982. His first years in office were marked by a conflict with his predecessor Ahmadou Ahidjo (who resigned and went into exile) and by the coup attempt of 6 April 1984, carried out by officers of the Republican Guard and put down after heavy fighting in Yaounde. It is the serious threat that came "shortly after" his accession (B).

The return to the multi-party system (A) dates from 1990, the Operation Ghost Towns (C) from 1991, and the Bakassi dispute (D) became a crisis in the mid-1990s.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: tension over the re-introduction of multi-party system in Cameroon.
the April 6th 1984 abortive coup d'etat.
the organisation of Operation Ghost Towns.
the Cameroon-Nigeria dispute over the Bakassi peninsula.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An outstanding foreign policy achievement of the Biya regime in Cameroon since 1982 has been:

*Options as printed:* A) the admission of Cameroon into the Commonwealth of Nations.   B) the hosting of the OAU summit in Yaounde.   C) the pacific resolution of the Bakassi Crisis with Nigeria.   D) the Maroua Accord.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three of the printed options belong to the Biya period: the admission of Cameroon into the Commonwealth (1995), the OAU summit held in Yaounde (1996) and the peaceful settlement of the Bakassi dispute (the judgment of the International Court of Justice of 2002 and the agreements that followed, up to 2008 for the withdrawal of Nigeria). The Maroua Accord, usually the Maroua Declaration of 1975 between Ahidjo and Gowon, belongs to the Ahidjo period. As three options can be defended and the word "outstanding" does not decide between them, no letter is retained.

A full answer names the achievements, dates them and explains why each one was important for the image and the security of Cameroon.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major successful strategy adopted by Britain in the campaign against the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade in West Africa was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the Act abolishing the slave trade in the British Empire (1807), Britain created the West Africa Squadron, a naval force that patrolled the coast, stopped and searched ships suspected of carrying slaves and freed the captives, who were mostly landed at Freetown. Combined with treaties with African rulers and other powers, this enforcement was the most effective action against the trade at sea.

The Abolition Laws (B) were necessary but only decided the policy, Sierra Leone (C) was a refuge for freed slaves and a naval base, and the spread of Christianity (A) was a result and an accompaniment of the campaign, not its main weapon.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the spread of Christianity in West Africa.
the enactment of the Abolition Laws.
the founding of Sierra Leone.
the deployment of the Naval Squadron to the coast of West Africa.

questions.enonce_markdown: The effectiveness of Christian missionary activities in Nigeria was principally due to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Nigeria the missions (the CMS, the Methodists, the Baptists, the Catholics and the Presbyterians in Calabar) built schools that gave Africans reading, writing and skills for employment as clerks, interpreters, teachers and traders. These schools were the main attraction for converts and the reason why the missions grew quickly. This is the factor generally given as the principal one (B).

The use of local languages (A, for instance the translations of Bishop Crowther) helped, but it was a means; legitimate trade (C) and the end of the slave trade (D) were part of the wider aims of the missionary movement and of the British government.

**Answer: B.**
themes: christian missionary activity in west africa

choix.texte: the use of local languages in evangelisation.
the promotion of the education of the indigenes.
the promotion of legitimate trading activities.
the eradication of the slave trade.

questions.enonce_markdown: A political motive for the 19th century Jihads in West Africa was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The jihads of the 19th century (Usman dan Fodio in Hausaland from 1804, Seku Ahmadu in Macina, Al-Hajj Umar in the western Sudan) had religious motives (to purify Islam and to remove pagan practices), social and economic motives (injustice, heavy taxes) and a political motive: to replace the existing rulers with Islamic states governed by the Sharia under a religious leader, that is, theocratic states.

Options A, B and D describe the religious motives, not the political one.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the introduction of orthodox Islam.
the abolition of paganic Islamic practices.
the desire to create theocratic states.
the decline of Islam.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following were the provisions of the Berlin Act of 1885 EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) the acknowledgement of existing colonial possessions in Africa.   B) the establishment of principles for European occupation of Africa.   C) the laying down of rules for European expansion into the hinterland.   D) the carving out of spheres of influence for European powers in Africa.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Berlin Act of 26 February 1885 provided for freedom of trade in the Congo basin, freedom of navigation on the Congo and the Niger, a declaration against the slave trade and rules for new occupations on the African coast: the occupation had to be effective and the other powers had to be notified. The Act did not itself divide Africa: the spheres of influence were drawn afterwards through bilateral treaties between the powers. The carving out of spheres of influence (D) is therefore the usual exception.

The question is, however, loosely worded: the Act did not really regulate the expansion into the hinterland either (C, the hinterland doctrine was invented by the powers afterwards), so the wording is not reliable enough for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: D (the carving out of spheres of influence for European powers in Africa).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Samori Toure was referred to as the Bonaparte of the Sudan mainly because:

*Options as printed:* A) he was the grandson of Napoleon.   B) of his ability to organise his Mandinka Empire.   C) of the alliances he forged with the Europeans.   D) of his military strategy against the French.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Samori Toure (c. 1830-1900) built the Wassoulou empire (the Mandinka empire) in the western Sudan from the 1860s and 1870s. He was compared to Napoleon for his military and organising talent: a trained, disciplined standing army, a well-organised administration and supply system, and a long resistance to French conquest until his capture in 1898. He was not related to Napoleon (A), and he fought the French rather than forging lasting alliances with Europeans (C).

The talent for organising the empire (B) and the military strategy against the French (D) are both part of the reason for the nickname, so two options can be defended and no letter is retained.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The effectiveness of the Abyssinian resistance against Italy at Adowa in 1896 was mainly attributed to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At Adowa (1 March 1896) the army of Menelik II destroyed an Italian force that had come to impose the Italian version of the Treaty of Wuchale (Ucciali). Menelik had united the nobles of the country behind him, bought modern rifles and guns from European powers, and used diplomacy and good intelligence. His leadership is the best single explanation.

Abyssinia was superior in numbers but not in technology (A); the national solidarity (B) was itself a result of Menelik's leadership; and the Italian mistakes (D, poor maps, divided columns) helped but were secondary.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the military superiority of Abyssinia.
the Abyssinian solidarity.
the leadership qualities of Emperor Menelik.
the incompetence of Italian soldiers.

questions.enonce_markdown: Assimilation was replaced by Association as a French colonial policy in Africa principally because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Assimilation aimed to turn Africans into Frenchmen, with French culture, French law and finally French citizenship. It was costly and hard to apply, and above all it would have made the Africans legally and politically equal to the French, which the colonial administrators and settlers would not accept. Association replaced it from the early 20th century: the Africans were to keep their own institutions and customs under French direction, and were treated as subjects without the rights of citizens.

The Africans did not choose Association (A); the criticism of French thinkers (C) existed but was not the decisive reason; and the aim of Assimilation was to educate Africans, not a problem in itself (D).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the Africans preferred Association to Assimilation.
Assimilation made all Africans equal to Frenchmen.
of the opposition to Assimilation by French intellectuals.
too many Africans were educated under Assimilation.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Second World War could be considered a blessing for the African Continent in that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The war weakened Britain and France, taught thousands of African ex-servicemen that Europeans could be beaten and that colonial claims about freedom were not applied at home, spread the ideas of the Atlantic Charter, and raised prices and hardship in the towns. The result was a much more militant nationalism after 1945, which led to independence in the following two decades. From the African point of view this is the "blessing" of the war (A).

The colonial powers did not carry out intensive development in the war years (B), the super powers did not simply replace them as rulers (C), and there was no free entry into Europe (D).

**Answer: A.**
themes: impact of world war two on africa

choix.texte: it resulted in the birth of militant nationalism.
the colonial powers carried out intensive economic development.
the European colonial powers were replaced by the Super Powers.
free entry was granted Africans into Europe as compensation for assistance in the war.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The rapid development of African nationalism shortly after 1945 was largely influenced by:

*Options as printed:* A) rising unemployment and hardship.   B) the Second World War.   C) Pan-Africanism.   D) the Super Powers.
questions.corrige_markdown:
African nationalism grew quickly after 1945 for several reasons that are commonly given together: the experience and the return of the ex-servicemen, the economic hardship, inflation and unemployment of the post-war years, the Fifth Pan-African Congress of Manchester in 1945 and the anti-colonial attitude of the United States and of the Soviet Union. The printed options each name one of these, and the word "largely" does not allow one to separate them with certainty (the Second World War is the wider cause and the question already says "after 1945"). No letter is retained.

A full answer explains how the war, the economic hardship, the Pan-African movement and the international situation worked together.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Ghana's early independence in 1957 could be attributed to the fact that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kwame Nkrumah founded the Convention People's Party (CPP) in 1949 after leaving the UGCC. The CPP organised the masses (Positive Action in 1950), won the elections of 1951, 1954 and 1956 and held together under his leadership, so that Britain had no alternative partner with comparable support and granted independence on 6 March 1957 (D).

The UGCC and the CPP were not reconciled; they split in 1949 (A). The CPP was not the only party, since the opposition parties such as the National Liberation Movement existed (B). The British did not see Nkrumah as easy to manipulate: he was imprisoned in 1950 before being released to lead the government (C).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the UGCC and CPP leadership were reconciled over Nkrumah's position.
the CPP was the only political party in the Gold Coast after 1949.
the British officials saw Nkrumah as a leader they could easily manipulate.
the CPP remained strong and united throughout the struggle.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major step undertaken by French colonial authorities to satisfy the political aspirations of the French African colonies in the 1950s was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Loi-Cadre (the Defferre framework law of 23 June 1956) gave the overseas territories universal suffrage, territorial assemblies with real powers and local governments with African ministers. It was the main concession of the 1950s to the political demands of the African elites.

The Brazzaville Conference took place in 1944 (A). The French Community was created by the Constitution of 1958 (C) as a framework intended to keep the territories linked to France; it is a later and more limited reform, but it also falls in the 1950s, which makes this question open to some discussion. The territorial assemblies already existed before the Loi-Cadre (D) and were given greater powers by it.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the convening of the Brazzaville Conference.
the adoption of the Loi-Cadre.
the creation of the French Community.
the creation of Legislative Assemblies.

questions.enonce_markdown: Neo-colonialism was manifested economically in the former French Equatorial Africa after 1960 through:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Neo-colonialism means that a former colonial power keeps control over a country that is formally independent. In the economic field, this was done through development aid, financial and technical dependence, the monetary arrangements of the franc zone and trade agreements that kept the economies of the former colonies tied to France. The provision of aid to sustain weak economies (D) is the only option that is economic.

Options A, B and C describe political and military forms of neo-colonialism.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the adoption of the pre-independence political system introduced by the French authorities.
the support of the French government to constitutional authorities.
the presence of French troops to safeguard the interest of the former colonial territories.
the provision of development aid to sustain the feeble economies of former colonies.

questions.enonce_markdown: The political drive behind most military coups in Nigeria has been:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for the political cause. The Nigerian coups (January and July 1966, 1975, 1983, 1985 and 1993) followed rivalries between politicians and regions, ethnic and regional tension, rigged or annulled elections (1965, 1983, 1993) and the dictatorial attitude of rulers, which is option A.

Options B and C are economic causes, and D mixes a religious and regional conflict with a social complaint; none of them is the political cause.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: political infighting, tribalism, elections malpractice and dictatorship.
mismanagement, mass unemployment, inflation and low wages.
the unbalanced distribution of wealth, excessive waste and capital flight.
conflict between the Muslim North and the Christian South and breakdown in basic necessities.

questions.enonce_markdown: The dismantling of the Apartheid system of government in South Africa was caused by the following factors EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The dismantling of apartheid began after the election of F.W. de Klerk as President in 1989: in February 1990 he freed Nelson Mandela and unbanned the ANC, and the main apartheid laws were repealed in 1991. It followed years of pressure from the UNO, the Commonwealth and others (sanctions, isolation). The election of Mandela as President came after the first non-racial elections of April 1994, when the system had already been dismantled, so it was a result and not a cause.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: pressure from the Commonwealth of Nations.
the election of F.W. De Klerk as President.
the election of Nelson Mandela as President.
pressure from the UNO.

questions.enonce_markdown: In the 1990s Rwanda became the focal point of international attention principally because of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The death of President Habyarimana in a plane crash on 6 April 1994 started the killings, but what drew the world's attention to Rwanda was the genocide that followed: in a few weeks hundreds of thousands of Tutsi and moderate Hutu were massacred, and the international community was criticised for failing to stop it. This is option C.

The assassination (A) was the trigger, and the political persecution (B) was part of the background; Rwanda was not known in the 1990s for famine as the main issue (D).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the assassination of President Juvenal Habyarimana.
political harassments and executions.
genocide.
persistent famine and drought.

questions.enonce_markdown: James II was tolerated by the English people until 1688 mainly because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
James II (King from 1685) was a Catholic, but the English Protestants accepted him because his heirs were his two Protestant daughters, Mary (married to William of Orange) and Anne, and he was no longer young. They expected his reign to be short. This changed in June 1688, when the birth of a Catholic son created a Catholic succession, and a group of leaders invited William of Orange to come and defend English liberties, which led to the Glorious Revolution.

James never promised to give up his religion (A) or to break with France (C), and his Declarations of Indulgence favoured Catholics and Dissenters rather than the Church of England (D).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: he had promised to abandon his Catholic Religion.
he was old and likely to be replaced by his protestant daughters.
he promised to cut off relations with Catholic France.
he showed much indulgence towards the Church of England.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Seven Years War was significant to the American War of Independence in that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Seven Years War (1756-1763; the French and Indian War in America) ended with the Treaty of Paris of 1763 by which France gave up Canada. The colonists no longer had to fear the French and their Indian allies on their borders, and so they no longer needed the protection of the British army. This relieved them of dependence on Britain and made them more ready to resist British measures later on.

The war showed British strength, not weakness (B); it was Britain, not the colonies, which came out of the war with a heavy debt (C); and the resources of the colonies were already well known (D).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: it relieved the Colonies from continuous dependence on Britain.
it exposed the weakness of Britain to the American Colonies.
it left the Colonies financially dependent on Britain.
it exposed the rich resources of the Colonies to Britain.

questions.enonce_markdown: British contribution to the collapse of the Congress System was evident in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Congress System (Aix-la-Chapelle 1818, Troppau 1820, Laibach 1821, Verona 1822) was meant to keep the peace of Europe, and the conservative powers wanted to use it to put down revolutions in other states. Britain, first under Castlereagh (State Paper of May 1820) and then under Canning, refused to accept the principle of collective intervention in the internal affairs of other countries and withdrew from the Congresses. This opposition broke the unity of the powers.

Britain did attend the first Congresses (A), formed no alliance with France against the other powers (B) and the Barbary Pirates were not involved (D).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: her refusal to attend the various Congresses.
her alliance with France against the other Congress Powers.
her outright rejection of intervention in internal revolts.
her support for the activities of the Barbary Pirates.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Bismarck's main objective in the Secret Reinsurance Treaty of 1887 was to:

*Options as printed:* A) consolidate German friendship with Austria.   B) bring his allies, Russia and Serbia, together.   C) consolidate the Triple Alliance of 1882.   D) consolidate the Dreikaiserbund Treaty.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Reinsurance Treaty was a secret agreement of June 1887 between Germany and Russia: each promised to stay neutral if the other was at war with a third power (except if Germany attacked France or Russia attacked Austria-Hungary). Bismarck made it after the Dreikaiserbund (the League of the Three Emperors, 1881) lapsed because of the rivalry of Austria and Russia in the Balkans. His aim was to keep Russia from allying with France and to avoid a war on two fronts. None of the printed options states this: Serbia was not an ally of Germany or a party to the treaty (B), the Triple Alliance and the friendship with Austria (A, C) were separate arrangements, and the Dreikaiserbund (D) was the older arrangement that the treaty replaced rather than consolidated. The nearest option is D, but the wording is defective and no letter is retained.

A full answer gives the terms, the date, the diplomatic situation after the lapse of the Dreikaiserbund and the failure to renew the treaty in 1890.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Germany's responsibility for the outbreak of the First World War was more evident in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo (28 June 1914), Germany gave Austria-Hungary its unconditional support (the "blank cheque" of early July 1914) in its action against Serbia, which encouraged Austria to refuse any compromise and made a general war in Europe much more likely. This is the strongest evidence of German responsibility.

The colonial and economic rivalries (A, C) and the secret diplomacy (D) were general causes shared by all the powers.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: her extension of the colonial rivalry with Britain and France.
her unconditional support to Austria-Hungary.
the rapid growth of her industries which led to economic rivalries.
her involvement in secret diplomatic negotiations in Europe.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An outstanding social impact of the Frist World War was that:

*Options as printed:* A) women were empowered.   B) lives were lost.   C) health care services were interrupted.   D) diseases were spread.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The First World War (1914-1918) had many social effects. Millions of soldiers and civilians were killed or wounded, families were broken, and in many countries women took over the work of the men, which helped them obtain the vote and a greater place in society after the war. The health services were disrupted and the influenza epidemic of 1918 spread widely. Both the loss of life (the most visible human cost) and the empowerment of women (the most lasting social change) can be called "outstanding", so the question cannot be marked with certainty and no letter is retained.

A full answer gives the human losses, the new role of women, the effect on health and the economic and political consequences.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Differences in objectives between the 'Big Five' at the Paris Peace Conference resulted in their inability to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Big Five (the USA, Britain, France, Italy and Japan) had conflicting aims: Wilson wanted a just peace based on the Fourteen Points and self-determination, Clemenceau wanted security and revenge on Germany, Lloyd George wanted a peace that would not ruin Germany and would protect British interests, and Italy and Japan wanted territory. The result was a compromise that satisfied nobody and treaties that were widely seen as unfair, above all to Germany.

The treaties were in fact concluded with all the defeated states (B false), Germany was disarmed to a large extent by the Treaty of Versailles (C), and the destruction of the Soviet regime was not a common aim of the conference (D).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: conclude fair and just peace treaties.
conclude peace treaties with the vanquished.
effectively disarm the defeated nations.
destroy the Communist regime in Russia.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most successful attempt at Collective Security outside the League of Nations in the 1920s was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Locarno Agreements of 1925 were negotiated outside the League. Germany, France and Belgium accepted their common frontiers and promised not to attack one another, with Britain and Italy as guarantors, and Germany was admitted to the League in 1926. This was the most successful attempt and gave rise to the "spirit of Locarno".

The Geneva Protocol (1924) and the Draft Treaty of Mutual Assistance (1923) were League proposals which were not accepted, and the Genoa Conference (1922) dealt with the economic reconstruction of Europe.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the Geneva Protocol of 1924.
the Genoa Conference of 1922.
the Locarno Agreements of 1925.
the Draft Treaty of Mutual Assistance of 1923.

questions.enonce_markdown: The flaws of the Paris Peace Settlement precipitated the outbreak of World War II in 1939 because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Germans called the Treaty of Versailles a "Diktat" because it was imposed on them without negotiation. Hitler came to power promising to cancel it: he rearmed Germany, remilitarised the Rhineland (1936), united Austria with Germany (1938), took the Sudetenland and then the rest of Czechoslovakia, and attacked Poland in September 1939. This is the direct link between the flaws of the peace settlement and the war.

Britain and France were not determined to defend the treaties; they followed a policy of appeasement (C). The attitudes of Italy and Russia (A, B) were less important.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Italy wanted to correct the errors in the Peace Treaties.
Russia was angry at her isolation during the peace talks.
Britain and France were determined to defend the treaties.
Hitler was resolved to cancel the 'Diktat' imposed on Germany.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main reason for America's entry into the Korean War of 1950 -1953 was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When North Korea invaded South Korea in June 1950, President Truman saw it as a communist advance to be stopped, in the same way as in Greece and Turkey under the Truman Doctrine. The USA brought the matter before the UN Security Council and led the UN force in order to apply the policy of containment of communism (D).

China entered the war only later, in the autumn of 1950, after UN forces crossed the 38th parallel (A), and the removal of Kim Il-Sung or the support of Syngman Rhee were means or consequences, not the main aim (B, C).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: to curb Chinese influence in the Korean peninsula.
to flush Kim Il-Sung out of power in North Korea.
to enforce Syngman Rhee's authority over Korea.
to enforce the Policy of Containment.

questions.enonce_markdown: Relaxation of international tension in the Cold War was expedient because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 the two super powers realised that a direct conflict could lead to a nuclear war that nobody could win. This led to the hot line (1963), the Test Ban Treaty (1963), the arms limitation talks of the 1970s and the policy of detente. The fear of nuclear war is the main reason (B).

The Sino-American rapprochement (A) was one of the results of detente, and the sovereignty of Germany (C) and the influence of the Third World (D) were minor factors.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the decision of China to join forces with the USA against the Soviet Union.
the threats of a nuclear war provoked by the Super Powers.
the determination of Germany to gain full sovereignty after 1950.
the growing influence of the Third World Countries in international politics.

questions.enonce_markdown: The inability of the UNO to bring lasting peace to some major conflicts in the world has been the result of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The UN can act only if its members agree, and the five permanent members of the Security Council can block any decision by veto. When the interests of a major power are involved (the Cold War conflicts, Palestine, Vietnam, later Syria and others) the Council is paralysed, or its action is limited. This is the main reason for the failures of the UN (B).

The lack of a permanent force and of funds (A, D) are real difficulties but they are themselves linked to the unwillingness of the powers to support the organisation, and the Security Council and the Assembly are not rivals in the same way (C).

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: lack of trained forces to intervene during such conflicts.
major power interests in such conflict areas.
conflict between the Security Council and the Assembly.
lack of finances to support intervention during such conflicts.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An important economic benefit of the Francophonie to its members has been:

*Options as printed:* A) the promotion of new technologies in information and communication.   B) the promotion of education through the award of scholarships.   C) the promotion of agriculture and livestock farming in some states.   D) the promotion of democratic practices and international peace.
questions.corrige_markdown:
La Francophonie is the organisation of French-speaking countries (the Agence de Cooperation Culturelle et Technique created in 1970, then the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie). It works for the French language, for education and culture, for communication technologies and, in its more recent period, for democracy and peace. Among the printed options only the support of agriculture and livestock (C) and the technologies of communication (A) can be called economic in a strict sense, and I could not confirm which one the examiners have in mind: the scholarships (B) are educational and democracy and peace (D) are political. No letter is retained.

A full answer separates the economic, cultural and political benefits and gives examples.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The immediate cause of the outbreak of the Arab-Israel Conflict of 1948-1949 was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The British mandate over Palestine ended on 14 May 1948. On that day the Jewish leaders proclaimed the State of Israel and on 15 May the armies of Egypt, Transjordan, Syria, Iraq and Lebanon entered Palestine. The proclamation of the State of Israel is therefore the immediate cause of the war.

The Jewish immigration (B), the promises made by Britain to the Arabs (C) and the activity of armed groups such as the Irgun and the Stern Gang (D) are long-term causes or part of the background.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the proclamation of the independence of Israel.
the massive influx of the Jews into Palestine.
the failure by Britain to respect her promise made to the Arabs.
the existence of the rival terrorist organisation.

questions.enonce_markdown: The rift between China and the Soviet Union was principally caused by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
After Stalin's death, Khrushchev denounced Stalin (1956) and proclaimed peaceful co-existence with the capitalist West. Mao Zedong saw this as a betrayal of Marxism-Leninism and a weakness towards the USA, and the quarrel (also about leadership of the communist world and the Soviet reluctance to help China with nuclear weapons) became open at the end of the 1950s and in the early 1960s. The policy of peaceful co-existence is generally given as the principal cause (D).

The Sino-American detente (B, 1971-1972) and the admission of China to the UN (C, 1971) came after the split and were partly its consequences, and the position of China as a third force (A) was a result of it.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the emergence of China as a Third Force in world politics.
the Sino-American Détente.
the admission of China into the UNO.
Khrushchev's policy of Peaceful Co-existence with the West.
